name: IB Connection
tagline: EdTech platform for IB Diploma students — organizational intelligence meets academic excellence
description: Full-stack platform helping IB students at Liceo de Cervantes Barranquilla manage coursework, deadlines, CAS tracking, and exam prep. Built with React, Node.js, PostgreSQL, and deployed on AWS. Features real-time collaboration, AI-powered study recommendations, and offline-first PWA.
longDescription: IB Connection was born from watching brilliant students drown in the complexity of the IB Diploma Programme. The platform centralizes everything: subject dashboards with progress tracking, CAS portfolio builder with reflection templates, EE/IA timeline manager, and a smart calendar that understands IB-specific deadlines. The backend uses a microservices architecture with GraphQL federation, enabling real-time updates across devices. PostgreSQL with row-level security handles multi-tenant data isolation. Deployed on AWS ECS with CloudFront CDN, achieving 99.9% uptime and <200ms p95 latency globally.

name: My Life OS
tagline: Gamified, AI-coached single-user life management — your operating system for intentional living
description: A comprehensive personal operating system combining PARA methodology, Zettelkasten knowledge management, habit tracking with streaks, goal decomposition (OKRs), journaling with AI insights, and life area dashboards. Built as a local-first web app with IndexedDB, optional Supabase sync, and a beautiful dark/light theme system.
longDescription: Life OS treats your life like a well-architected system. Four pillars: Projects (actionable outcomes with next actions), Areas (ongoing responsibilities with standards), Resources (curated knowledge with bidirectional links), Archives (completed/inactive). The AI coach analyzes patterns in your journaling, habits, and project velocity to suggest course corrections weekly. Habit system uses exponential backoff for missed days — no guilt spirals. Goals decompose from 10-year vision → yearly OKRs → quarterly rocks → weekly sprints → daily highlights. All data stays local (IndexedDB) with optional end-to-end encrypted Supabase sync. Built with SvelteKit, TypeScript, and a custom design system.

name: HTB Second Brain
tagline: Bilingual cognitive system for CJCA certification — Zettelkasten + PARA + CODE methodology
description: Obsidian-based knowledge management system designed for Hack The Box CJCA certification preparation. 500+ atomic notes covering web exploitation, privilege escalation, Active Directory, cloud security, and malware analysis. Bilingual (ES/EN) with spaced repetition integration, CTF writeup templates, and methodology cheatsheets.
longDescription: This isn't just a vault — it's a cognitive accelerator. Built on the CODE framework (Capture, Organize, Distill, Express) with PARA structure. Every HTB machine, Academy module, and certification topic gets a dedicated note with: attack path diagram (Mermaid), command reference, mitigation strategies, and cross-references to related concepts. Spaced repetition via Obsidian Spaced Repetition plugin ensures retention. Bilingual tags enable seamless context switching. Includes automated CTF writeup generator that produces publication-ready markdown from structured templates. The system reduced my CJCA prep time by ~40% compared to linear study.

name: NexusOS
tagline: Experimental distributed systems playground — exploring consensus, CRDTs, and edge computing
description: A research project implementing a distributed operating system prototype in Rust. Features: Raft consensus for metadata, CRDT-based file synchronization, WebAssembly runtime for edge functions, and a capability-based security model. Currently exploring conflict-free replicated data types for offline-first collaboration.
longDescription: NexusOS asks: what if the OS was distributed by default? The kernel coordinates a cluster of nodes running a modified WebAssembly runtime. Files are CRDTs (Yjs-inspired) — merge automatically, work offline, sync when online. Raft manages the namespace metadata (permissions, paths, versions). Capability-based security replaces ACLs: every syscall carries a capability token. The scheduler places WASM modules on nodes based on data locality, latency, and resource constraints. Written in Rust with async-std, tokio, and custom WASM host. Not production-ready — a learning vehicle for distributed systems, consensus, and language runtimes.

name: SearchTheBox
tagline: HTB machine search & writeup navigator — built with S4vitar's methodology
description: CLI tool and web interface for searching Hack The Box machines by difficulty, OS, tags, and release date. Integrates with HTB API for real-time data. Includes writeup templates following S4vitar's methodology, automated report generation, and a TUI for terminal lovers.
longDescription: Born from frustration with HTB's web UI during certification prep. SearchTheBox lets you filter machines like: `stb search --os linux --difficulty medium --tags active-directory,web --retired false`. The web UI adds visual difficulty heatmaps, tag co-occurrence networks, and a 'study path' generator that orders machines for optimal skill progression. Writeup templates enforce S4vitar's structure: Reconnaissance → Enumeration → Exploitation → Privilege Escalation → Post-Exploitation → Lessons Learned. Exports to PDF, Notion, Obsidian, and GitHub. Built with Go, Bubble Tea (TUI), and React (web).
